claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is susceptible to rapid oxidation or pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
The proposed intervention is a thin aluminum-rich diffusion coating produced by pack cementation and controlled heat treatment.
An aluminum-rich diffusion coating will improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr while maintaining its mechanical properties.
The coating will produce a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
Aluminum in the diffusion coating will preferentially oxidize during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential oxidation of aluminum will form a slow-growing protective alumina layer.
The alumina layer will act as a barrier to oxygen ingress and significantly reduce oxidation.
Reduced oxygen ingress will preserve the underlying bulk microstructure and mechanical properties.
Coated specimens will have significantly lower weight gain than untreated specimens.
Coated specimens will develop a thinner and more uniform oxide scale than untreated specimens.
After coating and oxidation exposure, the alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After coating and oxidation exposure, the alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr quickly undergoes oxygen-induced pesting under approximately 800 °C air exposure for 5 hours.
The oxidation-resistance improvement is expected in air from 800 to 1000 °C for exposures around 5 hours.
Mechanical-property retention is expected at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
